title: NEB Class 11 Chemistry — Aromatic Hydrocarbons — 2024
subject: chemistry
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State Huckel's rule. Explain why benzene is aromatic.
questions.solution:
**Huckel (4n+2) rule:** a planar, cyclic, conjugated system with (4n+2) π-electrons is aromatic.

Benzene: cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, 6 π-electrons (n = 1) — delocalised in a ring current. All C–C bonds equal (139 pm), with ~152 kJ/mol resonance stabilisation.
questions.knowledgeNote: Cyclobutadiene (4π) is anti-aromatic — same checklist, opposite verdict.

questions.question: Describe the mechanism of nitration of benzene.
questions.solution:
(1) Electrophile generation: HNO₃ + 2H₂SO₄ → NO₂⁺ + H₃O⁺ + 2HSO₄⁻.

(2) NO₂⁺ attacks the ring → resonance-stabilised σ-complex (carbocation).

(3) HSO₄⁻ removes a ring proton → aromaticity restored, **nitrobenzene**.

Conditions: conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄ at ~50°C.
questions.knowledgeNote: Electrophilic substitution (not addition) preserves the aromatic sextet — the motive of all benzene chemistry.

questions.question: What is Friedel-Crafts alkylation? Write one of its limitations.
questions.solution:
Benzene + alkyl halide with anhydrous AlCl₃ gives alkylbenzene: C₆H₆ + CH₃Cl → C₆H₅CH₃ + HCl (electrophilic substitution via R⁺).

**Limitation:** carbocation rearrangement (n-propyl → isopropyl products) and polyalkylation — the product activates further, so mixtures form.
questions.knowledgeNote: Acylation avoids rearrangement (acylium ion is resonance-stabilised) — the workaround NEB often asks next.

questions.question: What are ortho-para directors and meta directors? Give two examples of each.
questions.solution:
**o/p-directors** (activating, lone-pair donors): –OH, –NH₂, –CH₃, halogens (deactivating but o/p).

**m-directors** (deactivating, electron-withdrawing): –NO₂, –CHO, –COOH, –SO₃H.

Directing follows σ-complex stability — the electrophile enters where the positive charge avoids the substituent (meta) or is shared by it (ortho/para).
questions.knowledgeNote: Halogens are the odd ones: deactivating yet o/p-directing — the exception that proves the resonance rule.

questions.question: How is benzoic acid prepared from toluene? Write the reaction.
questions.solution:
Strong side-chain oxidation: **C₆H₅CH₃ + 3[O] (alkaline KMnO₄, heat) → C₆H₅COOH + H₂O**.

Any alkyl side chain, whatever its length, is chewed back to –COOH on the ring.
questions.knowledgeNote: Side-chain oxidation diagnoses alkylbenzenes — the surviving –COOH marks where the chain was attached.

questions.question: Draw the two Kekule structures of benzene. Why are all carbon–carbon bond lengths in benzene equal?
questions.solution:
Kekule: two cyclohexatriene forms with alternating double bonds shifted by one position.

Real benzene is the **resonance hybrid** — π-electrons delocalised over all six carbons, so every bond is identical (139 pm), between single (154) and double (134).
questions.knowledgeNote: Equal bond lengths killed Kekule's alternating structure experimentally — X-ray evidence for delocalisation.
